column3: The Hebrew repeats the Philistines, the ark of God, and Dagon. BSB carries the first two forward implicitly and replaces the final Dagon with “his statue.” The temple is literally Dagon’s “house.”

The Hebrew explicitly names Dagon’s head and the two palms of his hands as “cut off”; BSB uses “his head and his hands broken off.” In the concluding clause the Hebrew retains Dagon’s name, where BSB says “the torso.”
The Hebrew explicitly calls the threshold “Dagon’s threshold”; BSB leaves that possessive implicit.
The Hebrew repeats “the ark of the God of Israel” in the instruction about Gath; BSB uses “It.”
The Hebrew refers to moving “it”; BSB supplies “the ark to Gath.” It describes the affected men as “from small to great,” rendered “both young and old” in BSB.

The Hebrew repeats the ark of God and Ekron at its arrival; BSB uses “it” and leaves the destination implicit. The Ekronites speak collectively with singular “me” and “my people,” rendered plural “us” and “our people” in BSB.
The Hebrew again uses singular “me and my people”; BSB has “us and our people.” The hand of God is described as “very heavy there,” where BSB has “heavy upon it.”
